source: captured from spacepackets 0.32.0, an independent implementation
note: TM transfer frame primary headers emitted by spacepackets, a Python implementation of the CCSDS formats written from the standards by other authors. The primary header packs twelve fields into six octets with only two of them octet-aligned, so nearly every field shares a boundary with another and a shift off by one produces a header that still round-trips against itself. Every other tmdl vector is derived from the clause 4.1.2 layout; these octets are what catches a boundary two readers placed the same way and both got wrong. The capture program is not committed — it needs a dependency astro does not take — and the fields on each vector are what was asked of the other implementation.

encode.name: interop-scid-42-vc0-first-packet
encode.note: The baseline: spacecraft 42, virtual channel 0, a packet starting at the first octet of the data field. Sync flag set and segment length identifier 11, which clause 4.1.2.7.4 fixes for a frame carrying packets rather than a bitstream.

encode.name: interop-both-frame-counts-at-maximum
encode.note: Master channel and virtual channel frame counts both at 255. They are the two octet-aligned fields in the header, so this vector is the control: if it passes and the others fail, the error is in a bit boundary rather than in the field order.

encode.name: interop-spacecraft-id-1023-and-virtual-channel-7
encode.note: Both identifiers at the largest their fields hold, which pins where one ends and the next begins. The spacecraft ID is ten bits spanning octets 0 and 1, and the virtual channel ID is the three bits after it — so an implementation giving the spacecraft ID eleven bits or twelve passes the low-value vectors and fails this one.

encode.name: interop-operational-control-field-flag
encode.note: The OCF flag, which is the single bit closing octet 1 immediately after the virtual channel ID.

encode.name: interop-frame-secondary-header-flag
encode.note: The secondary header flag, the top bit of the data field status. Paired with the OCF vector this fixes two single-bit flags that sit five octets apart and are easy to transpose.

encode.name: interop-first-header-pointer-2046-idle-frame
encode.note: First header pointer 2046, which clause 4.1.2.7.6 reserves to mean the frame carries only idle data. It is one of two reserved values at the top of an eleven-bit field, so it also pins the field's width.

encode.name: interop-first-header-pointer-2047-no-packet-starts
encode.note: First header pointer 2047, the other reserved value: no packet starts in this frame, because a packet from an earlier frame is still being carried. Confusing this with 2046 loses idle-frame detection, and both encode as all-ones in a field whose width has to be exactly right.

encode.name: interop-first-header-pointer-mid-frame
encode.note: A first header pointer of 100 on virtual channel 1: an ordinary value in the middle of the field, so the reserved-value vectors above are not the only evidence for its width or position.
